Usage:   discern <command> [options]

Description:

  Give each task its own worktree, a separate checkout and branch, and check its
  work with your project's gate, its full quality check, before it lands. New
  here? `discern setup` explains the first step, and `discern setup begin`
  starts setting discern up in this project.

Options:

  -h, --help              - Show this help.
  -V, --version           - Print the installed discern version.
  --json                  - Print the result as one JSON document on stdout.
  --markdown              - Print the result as one Markdown document on stdout.
  --render                - Print the Markdown result formatted for the
                          terminal.
  --no-color              - Turn off color. discern also leaves color off when
                          `NO_COLOR` is set to any non-empty value, when `TERM`
                          is `dumb`, or when output isn't a terminal.
  --plain                 - Turn off prompts, paging, the full-screen reader,
                          and live progress, and print static output. discern
                          also skips prompts in CI, with `--json`, `--markdown`,
                          or `--render`, and when input or output isn't a
                          terminal.
  --theme <theme:string>  - Choose colors for a `light` or `dark` terminal, or
                          `auto`. Default: `auto`, which asks an interactive
                          terminal for its background color and assumes dark
                          when it can't tell. `--no-color` and `NO_COLOR` skip
                          that check.

Commands:

━━ ▲ YOUR DESK ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
— you use these in an interactive terminal
    desk         Open the desk, your interactive view of every task in this
                 project.
    enter        Open a shell in another worktree, in the same folder you're in
                 now.

━━ ▲ AGENTIC LOOP ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
— your coding agent runs these as it works
    status       Show where this checkout stands and what to do next.
    prepare      Run the quick checks while you work: fix and regenerate files,
                 then run the read-only checks, without tests.
    done         Run the gate on a clean, committed tree and record Proof when
                 it passes. The gate is your project's full quality check: the
                 jobs it configures, such as format, lint, type-check, and
                 tests.
    test         Run your project's tests on their own, without the rest of the
                 gate.
    progress     Check on a long operation, such as `discern done`, after losing
                 track of it.
    queue        Run a command, such as a test suite, once a test-run slot is
                 free, so parallel tasks don't overload this machine.
    tidy         Format the files discern manages: the map, the TODO list, your
                 instruction files, and `discern.toml`.

━━ ▲ WORKTREE LIFECYCLE ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
— your agent starts, updates, and lands each task with these
    start        Create a worktree for a new task: a separate checkout on its
                 own branch, started from the trunk (`main`), your project's
                 shared branch.
    update       Merge the latest trunk (`main`), your project's shared branch,
                 into this branch, and refresh what depends on it. For a newer
                 discern, use `discern upgrade`; for agent files alone, use
                 `discern refresh`.
    await        Wait for another task: until its work passes the gate, until it
                 lands, or until the trunk moves.
    accept       Land this worktree's proven commit on the trunk (`main`), your
                 project's shared branch.
    worktree     Manage worktrees: separate checkouts, each on its own branch,
                 for one task.
    identity     Print a stable value discern derives for a checkout's branch,
                 development host, port, database, and external resources.

━━ ▲ PROJECT SCRIPTS ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
— your project's own scripts, listed or run by name
    scripts      List your project's scripts, or run one by name.

━━ ▲ SETUP & MAINTENANCE ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
— you or your agent set up, check, and look after discern
    upgrade      Bring this project up to date with the discern you have
                 installed. To bring the trunk into a task branch, use `discern
                 update`; to regenerate agent files only, use `discern refresh`.
    doctor       Check that discern is installed correctly and that Git is set
                 up safely for it.
    config       Read, explain, and edit `discern.toml`, keeping its comments.
    refresh      Regenerate your agent files, skills, agent integrations, and
                 ADR index from their sources. To bring the trunk into this
                 branch, use `discern update`; to update the project for a newer
                 discern, use `discern upgrade`.
    uninstall    Remove discern's wiring from this project, and keep the files
                 you wrote.

━━ ▲ INSPECT & EXPLORE ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
— reports, reviews, and documentation for you or your agent
    improvement  Find the most valuable improvement to make next in how this
                 project uses discern.
    standards    Measure your project's standards: limits on measured numbers,
                 such as test coverage or bundle size. A change can tighten a
                 limit, but loosening one needs the owner's approval.
    checkpoints  Show the checkpoints that apply to this task, whether each
                 question has an answer, and which ones the current change would
                 trigger.
    skills       Manage skills, the reusable playbooks your agents follow: list
                 them, or copy a built-in one so you can edit it.
    impact       Show which scopes this branch's changes touch, and so which
                 scope gates `discern done` will run. Scopes are named regions
                 of the repository, set in `discern.toml`.
    coupling     Find files that usually change together in your Git history, so
                 a change doesn't miss one.
    patterns     Show patterns in how this project uses discern, from its local
                 logbook.
    map          Browse your project's map, the documentation your agents keep
                 about how the project works, or read one page by name.
    docs         Browse discern's manual, which comes with discern, or read one
                 page by name.
    help         Show help for discern, or for one command, such as `discern
                 help worktree prune`.
    licenses     Print discern's licenses and notices, and the notices for the
                 third-party software built into it.
    releases     Open discern's release notes in your browser, to see what's new
                 and whether a newer discern is out.
    mcp          Run discern's MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, which gives
                 coding agents discern's main commands as tools.

Examples:

  Orient yourself              discern status
  Agent in the main checkout?  discern start → (move into the worktree path it
                               prints...) → discern status → (write and commit
                               code...) → discern done → report ready for review
  Agent in a worktree?         (write and commit code...) → discern done →
                               report ready for review

Run `discern <command> --help` for detail on any command.
